images.caption: Figure 1:WorldBridgegenerates coherent 3D worlds from scattered reference images with little or no visual overlap. It preserves observed content while plausibly generating unseen regions, and supports (a) sparse-view scene reconstruction, (b) layout control through reference camera poses, (c) text-guided generation of unseen content, and (d) bridging references spanning real and imaginary visual styles.

Figure 2:Overview of WorldBridge.The scene encoder aggregates scattered references into a global representation, which the scene reader aligns to each view under RGB supervision. The diffusion transformer combines these features with encoded temporal and spatial references and text to generate RGB and geometry.
Figure 3:Temporal and spatial reference attention.All view pairs use camera encoding; temporal RoPE is omitted for interactions involving spatial references.

Figure 4:Overview of the WorldBridge benchmark.Short evaluates two-view bridging; Long evaluates long-range generation from six references; Agent uses synthetic scenes with on- and off-trajectory references. Right: WorldBridge shows a much higher fraction of reference pairs with less than 1% overlap than the public benchmarks, evaluating world generation with low-overlapping references.

Figure 5:Qualitative comparisons.Top: novel views on public NVS benchmarks and WorldBridge-Short. Bottom: point clouds and local details on WorldBridge-Long/Agent. The Long reference scene is estimated with DA3. Orange numbers indicate PSNR.
Figure 9:More qualitative results of the public NVS benchmarks[104,49].
Figure 13:More visualizations of sparse reconstruction by WorldBridge.
Figure 14:More visualizations of layout control by WorldBridge.
Figure 15:More visualizations of text control by WorldBridge.
Figure 16:For each spatial reference, four target arcs span 80%, 60%, 40%, and 20% mean reference-to-target coverage. Columns show the same frame indices along each arc.

Figure 17:Given two references and a target camera, we compare the held-out target, the scene reader RGB prediction, the local-only output, and the output with both branches. The last column visualizes the scene reader features at the target camera.
